provenance.hash_definition: SHA256 of ordered (column,dtype) JSON and pandas hash_pandas_object(index=False) bytes; pandas-version dependent
queries: SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows FROM observations
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT DISTINCT * FROM observations)
SELECT COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE "X" IS NULL), COUNT(DISTINCT "X") FROM observations
SELECT AVG("X"), STDDEV_SAMP("X"), MIN("X"), QUANTILE_CONT("X", 0.25), MEDIAN("X"), QUANTILE_CONT("X", 0.75), MAX("X"), COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE NOT ISFINITE("X")) FROM observations
SELECT COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE "T" IS NULL), COUNT(DISTINCT "T") FROM observations
SELECT AVG("T"), STDDEV_SAMP("T"), MIN("T"), QUANTILE_CONT("T", 0.25), MEDIAN("T"), QUANTILE_CONT("T", 0.75), MAX("T"), COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE NOT ISFINITE("T")) FROM observations
SELECT COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE "Y" IS NULL), COUNT(DISTINCT "Y") FROM observations
SELECT AVG("Y"), STDDEV_SAMP("Y"), MIN("Y"), QUANTILE_CONT("Y", 0.25), MEDIAN("Y"), QUANTILE_CONT("Y", 0.75), MAX("Y"), COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE NOT ISFINITE("Y")) FROM observations
SELECT "T" AS treatment, COUNT(*) AS n FROM observations GROUP BY "T" ORDER BY "T" LIMIT 30
SELECT "T", AVG("X"), VAR_SAMP("X") FROM observations WHERE "T" IN (0,1) GROUP BY "T" ORDER BY "T"

estimates.assumptions: Additive linear conditional mean; HC3 heteroskedasticity-robust normal interval. A constant effect or correct additive outcome specification is required.
Horvitz-Thompson ATE; correctly specified logistic propensity; propensity clipped at [0.01,0.99]. Stratified pairs bootstrap (80 refits), percentile interval.

Parametric augmented IPW with logistic treatment model and separate linear outcome models. The point estimate is doubly robust under a correct propensity or outcome model; the displayed simple influence-score interval additionally needs both parametric nuisance models correct (or negligible nuisance bias) and regularity.

Cross-fitted interactive-regression-model ATE / orthogonal AIPW score; 5 stratified folds, random-forest outcomes and logistic propensity. Asymptotic influence-score interval needs nuisance-rate and overlap assumptions; finite-sample coverage is not guaranteed.

association.assumptions: Unadjusted difference in sample means; association alone does not establish causality.

placebo.assumptions: One seeded treatment permutation; detects gross estimator artifacts, cannot validate exchangeability.

subset.assumptions: Seeded 80% subset stability check; not an independent replication.

refutation.interpretation: Passing a refutation check does not prove the causal assumptions. A failed check prompts investigation.

sensitivity.model: Single omitted-variable linear-model bias envelope using specified partial R-squared values (Cinelli & Hazlett, 2020).
sensitivity.interpretation: User-specified confounder strengths, not measured hidden confounding. Bounds cover point-estimate bias in either sign; they are not confidence or causal identification intervals.

limitations: Identification is conditional on the supplied graph and accepted scientific assumptions, not established by observational fit.
Only complete-data binary-treatment backdoor ATEs are supported; latent-variable ID and partial-identification bounds are not implemented.
Population transport, measurement error, selection bias and interference cannot be ruled out by these diagnostics.
Estimator agreement does not establish causal validity. Confidence intervals quantify sampling uncertainty under estimator assumptions, not uncertainty in the graph.
Individual counterfactuals are not identified by an ATE analysis; no individual counterfactual outcomes are generated.

identification.reason: The supplied adjustment set satisfies the backdoor criterion in the user-confirmed DAG, conditional on the accepted assumptions.

optimization.objective: mean(normalized regret + 0.20 query Brier + 0.04 capped cost-to-95 / budget)
optimization.selection: Train nine parameter settings; choose among training top three using validation only.

limitations: Four known-parameter linear-Gaussian candidate SCMs, not unrestricted graph discovery
95% intervals are finite-model Bayesian credible envelopes, not general frequentist confidence intervals
Query-EIG is a myopic finite-model adaptation of goal-oriented Bayesian design, not a reproduction of GO-CBED's transformer policy
No claim of state-of-the-art performance or universal scientific novelty
Misspecification is deliberately outside the model family and reports abstention/calibration failures
config.default_sync_note: Default policy synchronized to independently selected validation parameters after evaluation; all episodes explicitly supplied the same selected parameters.

benchmarks.conclusion: Study 1: the optimized nominal policy exactly matched query information gain per cost. Study 2: validity-aware experiment selection reduced weak-confounding false claims from 21/96 to 6/96 against the same-guard nominal acquisition; it tied validity decision-value and did not improve the stronger unseen-negative scenario.
